key_insight: Bi-stable nonlinear energy sinks (BNESs) passively redirect vortex-induced vibration energy away from dominant cable motion, reducing both vibration amplitude and drag-related energy in subsea cables.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical retrofit-style mitigation strategy for subsea power cables operating in unsteady currents, with potential to improve fatigue life and reduce flow-induced loading.
method: Integrated BNES attachments into the open-source MoorDyn cable model
Ran fully 3D time-domain simulations with Morison-type hydrodynamic forcing and spatially/temporally varying currents
Used data-driven optimization across multiple current profiles to tune BNES designs
evidence_signal: Across the sampled design space and current cases, optimized BNES configurations consistently reduced peak-to-peak vibration, cumulative VIV energy intake, and drag energy.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful tuning to the cable and flow regime, so benefits may not transfer directly without re-optimization for different currents or operating conditions.
paper_title: Bi-stable Nonlinear Energy Sinks (BNESs) for Response Mitigation and Drag Reduction of Subsea Cables Undergoing Vortex-induced Vibrations
